subject: Prod alert: Authentication gateway causing 5xx/429 spike — suspected token validation noise and retry cascade
messages:
From: Ella Torres <ella@acme-ml.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prod alert: Authentication gateway causing 5xx/429 spike — observed since 08:40 UTC

Hi team,

We're seeing a sudden spike of 5xx and 429 responses hitting our inference endpoints that go through Redwood's hosted gateway. The spike started ~08:40 UTC and has been intermittent but sustained for ~30m. Symptoms:
- Increased 5xx rate (internal metric: request_errors_5xx up ~2.6x)
- 429s appear correlated with queued retries on our side when requests time out
- A subset of failures look like token validation failures (401-ish semantics), but the gateway surfaces them as 5xx/timeout in our traces

Attached: auth_gateway_trace.txt (sample traces + request IDs) and a short summary of affected endpoints.

Impact: customer-facing latency elevated, several production jobs timed out and retried aggressively which made the 429s worse. We're starting to see user-facing errors. Can you confirm receipt and whether Redwood has any immediate mitigations?

Thanks,
Ella Torres
SRE, Acme ML
ella@acme-ml.com
Attachments: auth_gateway_trace.txt (text)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Torres <ella@acme-ml.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-11T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod alert: Authentication gateway causing 5xx/429 spike — observed since 08:40 UTC

Hi Ella — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the traces. We see the alert in our platform (routing + gateway). I'm triaging now and looping in infra/edge. Immediate plan:

- Enable a soft-fail validator on the gateway to classify token validation issues as 401/403 instead of returning 5xx where possible (reduces retry amplification).
- Short-term: increase backoff recommendations and add stricter client-side jitter in our guidance to your SREs.
- Collect: please share 3 example request IDs from the attached traces (we already pulled the first two) and any recent IdP change logs on your side (key rotation, clock changes).

I'll update in the next 15m with actions and temporary mitigations.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-03-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note: Acme ML production spike — need approval for temporary capacity routing + credits

Marcus / Laura — escalating for exec visibility. Acme ML is reporting elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts across inference traffic. Preliminary triage points to misclassified token validation failures at the auth gateway that propagated into retries and a queue saturation event. We've started hot mitigations (soft-fail validator, short-circuiting retriers) but traffic is still noisy.

Asks:
- Approve a temporary cross-region fallback (route some traffic to dedicated cluster in us-west) if needed — estimated cost impact ~$5k/day while active.
- Approve a customer credit conversation (they're in renewal cadence; want to keep it calm).

I can brief you both on the technical details now; putting Rishi on technical lead.

Thanks,
Dev
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Ella Torres <ella@acme-ml.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod alert: Authentication gateway causing 5xx/429 spike — suspected token validation noise and retry cascade

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 09:12, Ella Torres <ella@acme-ml.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sudden spike of 5xx and 429 responses ... A subset of failures look like token validation failures (401-ish semantics), but the gateway surfaces them as 5xx/timeout in our traces

Quick technical update from infra triage: we validated the following from traces + internal logs:
- Root cause (probable): upstream IdP performed a key rotation ~08:30 UTC. A small percentage of JWTs were issued with nbf timestamps ~30s in the future for clients whose clocks differ slightly (clock skew).
- Problem in our gateway: token validation library raised an unexpected exception path for those JWTs (we expected a deterministic 401), which bubbled up to a 5xx path in the gateway under a rare code path; that error also triggered request retries inside our fronting proxy.
- Amplification: client-side retries + proxy-level retries created a retry cascade that saturated per-host queues -> increase in 429s and timeouts.

Measures we've taken (live):
- Hotfix deployed: classify JWT validation exceptions as 401/403 where applicable (no longer map to 5xx).
- Increased token clock-tolerance to +/- 5 minutes for verification to absorb minor client clock skew while we coordinate with IdP.
- Temporarily increased request queue depth and enabled short-circuit handling for known token-validation request IDs to avoid retry amplification.
- Collected full request dump (attached acme_error_logs.zip) and created Jira SUP-8739 to track the RCA and follow-ups.

Initial impact reduction observed: 5xx rate down ~70% within 10 minutes of hotfix; 429s decreased as queues drained. Continuing to monitor.

Attachments: acme_error_logs.zip (logs, request IDs)

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Torres <ella@acme-ml.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-12T17:49:00-07:00
Subject: Close: root cause identified and mitigations applied — follow-up meeting scheduled

Hi Ella — final note to close the immediate incident:

Summary:
- Root cause: IdP key rotation + a small portion of JWTs emitted with future nbf timestamps combined with our gateway incorrectly surfacing validation exceptions as 5xx. That led to client and proxy retries which caused queue saturation and increased 429s/timeouts.
- Actions taken: hotfix to remap token validation exceptions to 401/403; increased verification clock tolerance; temporary queue and routing adjustments; guidance sent to Acme SRE for client backoff/jitter.

Next steps:
- Full RCA and postmortem doc in Jira SUP-8739 (link above).
- Proposed customer remedy: one month of platform credits and a joint postmortem call.
- Follow-up call scheduled: 2027-03-13T10:00:00-07:00 (Acme SREs + Redwood infra + account team).

Thanks for your patience and for the quick data — the logs you sent were crucial. We'll follow up with the PM/CS teams about credits and any contractual concerns.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
